$comment: Test fixture: five resources between them exercising every recipe role against testdata/shapes/widgets.json. `widget` is the full lifecycle (create, two reads, a mutation, map-shaped tags, an authored operation, list, delete); `cog` is setup-only and its create cannot be bound, so `spare`, which requires it, has its whole group refused with setup-refused; `gauge` is pre-existing and shows that such a resource carries more than its read; `sprocket` requires `gauge`, verifies its create with an authored assertion rather than a derived read-back, carries list-shaped tags, and is declared async so every clause that calls the service again — authored ones included — is wrapped in `eventually`.

neverProbe.GetWidgetSecret: Rotates the secret it returns, so the read verb in its name is a lie; every later reader of the old secret is broken by the call.
neverProbe.PurgeWidgets: Purges every widget in the account and cannot be undone. It takes no identifier, so no curated literal could make the call miss; the only safe probe is none.

allowProbe.PingWidgets: A liveness check: it takes no input, changes nothing, and returns the service's own status.
allowProbe.ScanWidgets: A read AWS happens to spell with a different verb, as DynamoDB does with Scan; it lists widgets and changes nothing.

operations.$comment: PolishWidget returns nothing, so its own response says nothing about whether it worked; the read-back is the whole assertion. The resource is not async, so the clause is emitted as written.

resources.$comment: Setup-only, and deliberately unbindable: CreateCog.Name is a patterned string with no bind, no matching export and no curated literal, so instantiating this resource is refused and every group that requires it is refused with it.

A second widget, complete in itself, whose only problem is that it requires `cog`. Its group is refused as setup-refused:cog before a single test is emitted — the refusal names the resource that could not be set up, and the operation it names is the create that would otherwise have been fine.
Pre-existing: no create, no delete, and its exports come from its read. Its group is not that read alone — an authored operation binding one of those exports gets a test of its own.

Requires the pre-existing gauge, whose read runs in setup and whose ARN the sprocket records. The create is verified by an authored assertion instead of the derived read-back, and `async` wraps that authored clause — it calls the service again — while leaving the responseField clause beside it alone.
